title: Rock Star Jack Antonoff Says Everyone Agrees: 'This Version of Modernity Is Trash'
summary:
Have you ever felt like the world is moving too fast and nobody is really happy? Jack Antonoff, the singer from the rock band Bleachers, thinks almost everyone feels that way. His new album, called *everyone for ten minutes*, is all about that feeling.

Antonoff says he wrote the album because people have never been more divided. But there's one thing we all agree on: "this version of modernity is trash." That means the way we live right now, with phones and screens everywhere, isn't making us have a good time.

He noticed something cool, though. More people are going to movie theaters, buying vinyl records, and going to concerts. It's like we're all craving real connections again, the kind you can touch and feel.

Antonoff remembers playing in tiny bars for just nine people when he was younger. He says that joy never left him. Now, even when he plays huge shows, he tries to see every fan as an individual with their own story.

The album also talks about sad things, like losing someone you love. Antonoff's sister died when he was 18, and he says talking about death is almost taboo—like it's a secret. But he puts those feelings into his music.

On the happier side, he sings about marrying actress Margaret Qualley. In one song, he describes being inside their wedding, surrounded by the people they love most, while the outside world didn't matter. Antonoff says his band is for anybody, but not everybody. It's a special club for people who get it.
why_it_matters: This story matters because you might also sometimes feel that too much screen time makes it harder to have real fun with friends, and it's okay to want more hands-on activities.

keywords.explanation: Modernity means the way we live today with all our new technology and fast-paced life.
Divided means people are separated into groups that disagree with each other.
Vinyl records are big black discs that play music on a special player, and many people enjoy their warm sound.
Taboo describes a topic that people feel is uncomfortable or secret to talk about.
Craving means wanting something very, very much.
An individual is one separate person, not part of a group.

background_read: Jack Antonoff is a well-known music producer who has worked with stars like Taylor Swift and Lorde, in addition to being the lead singer of Bleachers.
Vinyl records became rare after CDs and digital music took over, but recently many people have started buying them again because they love their unique sound.
Many adults also worry that spending too much time on phones and screens stops us from enjoying real-world activities with friends.
Article_Structure: WHO: Jack Antonoff, the singer from the rock band Bleachers.
WHAT: He says everyone agrees that modern life with phones and screens isn't making us happy, and his new album *everyone for ten minutes* is about this feeling.
WHERE: In his album and at his concerts, where he tries to connect with fans as individuals.
WHY: Because he sees people craving real, touchable experiences like vinyl records and concerts, away from screens.

perspectives.description: Some people love Antonoff's message because it reminds us to put down our phones and enjoy real experiences like concerts and records.
Others think he is just complaining; technology also connects us to friends and gives us access to music and information.
Many music fans simply enjoy the catchy tunes and don't think too much about the deeper message.
